Because all phenomena are without cause, due to the non-arising of all phenomena, one attains non-arising and non-ceasing. Due to non-arising and non-ceasing...
One immediately attains the non-apprehension of signs. Because of the non-apprehension of signs, one immediately attains the absence of arising and abiding.
Because of the absence of arising and abiding, one immediately attains stainlessness. Because of stainlessness, one immediately attains peerless awakening.

Because of peerless awakening, one immediately attains the absence of grasping and rejecting. Because of the absence of grasping and rejecting, one immediately attains equanimity beyond verbal expression.
Because it is equal and beyond verbal expression, one attains that which is without cause and without effect, in accord with *prajñā*, and is non-apprehending.
By means of skillful means (*upāya*), one enters the ultimate truth (*paramārtha*) and realizes the *dharmadhātu-tathatā*. This constitutes the recitation of *samādhi*.
If one uses ordinary skillful means, by reciting [the mantra] one hundred thousand times, one dreams of vomiting black substances; by two hundred thousand times, one dreams...
In this state of excellent realization, even for those whose transgressions are most grave, seventy thousand recitations will extinguish their sins and give rise to merit.
Regarding this recitation of samādhi, one should accord with the principle of the true nature (*dharmatā*) in each and every syllable of the mantra.

It does not require the use of a rosary or a fixed number of repetitions as a limit; rather, it is the gateway of realizing the principle, wherein the mind remains undistracted and abides in the yoga of the *iṣṭadevatā*.
This is the limit. Its efficacy is most rapid.
If one wishes to know future events, first smear a small altar. Have a youth of auspicious appearance bathe and change his clothes.
Consecrate incense with the mantra and smear it upon the youth’s hands; consecrate flowers and place them in his hands.

[The practitioner] covers the face of the boy and stands within the mandala. Furthermore, having separately empowered the flowers, he strikes the back of the boy’s hand once for each repetition, up to twenty-one times. He then asks about matters of good and evil, and the boy speaks them all.
Furthermore, there is another method: take a bright mirror and place it in the center of the maṇḍala. Empower it with flowers one hundred and eight times, and then recite the mantra.
With each recitation, cast a flower once upon the surface of the mirror; immediately, characters will appear upon the mirror's surface.
Regarding the discourse on good and evil matters:
if a child cries at night, have a young maiden twist thread clockwise, empower it with the mantra, and tie twenty-one knots.
When fastened beneath the neck, the crying will immediately cease.
If one suffers from a disease caused by malevolent spirits, one should empower white mustard seeds one hundred and eight times and strike the patient with them;
when this is done twenty-one times, the spirit will immediately flee.
Construct a mandala using cow dung and draw the form of a malevolent spirit on the ground with flour and charcoal.
Empower a branch of pomegranate and lash the spirit with it; that spirit will immediately weep and flee.

Furthermore, if the patient is in a distant location and unable to come in person, one should take either a willow branch, a peach branch, or a flower, empower it one hundred and eight times, and carry it to the patient's side; then, using the branch, one should brush the patient.
Have the patient smell flowers, or strike the patient with flowers; immediately the spirits will depart and the illness will be cured.
For those suffering from abscesses, swellings, or bites by venomous insects, empower sandalwood juice, mix it with earth to form a paste, and apply it to the wound; it will then heal.
If a woman is childless, one should write this mantra with ox-gall on birch bark and have her wear it.

Or, if a woman’s husband does not respect her, one should take a new flask, fill it with water, place within the flask the seven precious gems, various efficacious medicines, the five grains, and white mustard seeds; then tie a silk cloth around the neck of the flask.
Consecrate with the mantra one hundred and eight times. Have the woman form the root mudrā and place it upon her head;
by sprinkling water for consecration, she will immediately gain favor, love, and respect, and shall also bear children.
If one recites it one *koṭi* times atop a high mountain peak, Vajrapāṇi Bodhisattva will take this person [under his protection].
One enters the palace of the asuras, where one’s lifespan lasts for one kalpa. There, one beholds Maitreya, hears the True Dharma, and attains the stage of non-retrogression.
[Next is] the ritual for the maṇḍala of the mantra of the frowning Bhṛkuṭī-Vijayā Bodhisattva (the procedure for prostration and visualization is the same as above).
The World-Honored One entered the *Ākāśagarbha-parama-vajra-samādhi* and brought forth the Bodhisattva Bhṛkuṭī.
He then proclaimed this great Dharma, the nectar-like mantra, which all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas praised with joy, while non-Buddhists and celestial Māras were struck with terror.
All sentient beings of the six realms who heard it gave rise to the bodhicitta. At that time, on the earth...
Upon hearing this, all those in prison were able to cease their suffering. First, extend the two little fingers of both hands, each resting on the back of its respective ring finger.
Next, extend the two ring fingers, each resting on the back of its respective middle finger.
Bring the two wrists together, stand the two middle fingers so that their tips touch, and stand the two thumbs and two index fingers; however, slightly bend the tips of the index fingers.
With a gesture as if not yielding, move the index fingers back and forth.

The mantra is: Namaḥ sarvatathāgatebhyo viyūha-raśmivyo-ma-samuditebhyaḥ | Oṃ vāhana || *Namo sarvatathāgatebhyo viyūha-raśmivyo-ma-samuditebhyaḥ | Oṃ vāhana* (1) *Raḥ-vi-ya-samaya-samudite-vi-ya* (2) *Oṃ* (3) *vāhana* (4)
Śamaya (4) | Tārasatva tārasvayaṃtara sī (5) | Nṛkuti tiṭi (6) veṭi veṭi (7) | Velaṭi velaṭi (8) | Śvetijarājñe svāhā ||
Vāha (9). Use white silk; in the center, paint Śākyamuni, with Vajrapāṇi on the left and Avalokiteśvara on the right. That Buddha is golden in color.
He resembles a youth of sixteen years. To the left of Avalokiteśvara, one should paint Bhṛkuṭī (who resides in the stone of the Buddha).
Her form is like that of a celestial maiden (*devī*); her body is entirely white in color. She has three eyes and four arms: her first right hand holds a staff, the second holds a rosary;
her first left hand holds a flask, and the second holds a lotus. Her garments are red and white, and her countenance is exceedingly beautiful.
Correct. He wears a flower crown on his head. Below him, next, draw the vidyādhara kneeling in the Indian fashion (*hukuei*), holding an incense burner in his hand and gazing up at the Noble One.
The practitioner, from the first day of the waxing moon until the fifteenth day, should eat a porridge of barley and milk.
Constantly recite the mantra until the eighth day of the dark fortnight. For three days and three nights, abstain from food.
At the time of making offerings to the image, the image will emit light that enters into the toes of the Buddha’s feet. When this sign is seen, all heart-wishes will be fulfilled.
This is the power of the mantra: it can summon all nāgas, yakṣas, asuras, and others, causing them all to appear before one.
If one recites it one *koṭi* times, one will be able to subdue all māras, skillfully accomplish all rites of siddhi,
and likewise subjugate obstructive and wicked persons, causing them to be destroyed so that their evil deeds do not succeed.
There is one dharma for entering the palace of the asuras: for eight years, recite the mantra three thousand times every day while forming the Three-Eyed Seal.
With both hands, join the index fingers and little fingers, crossing them back-to-back and inserting them into the palms.
Straighten the two index fingers so they touch at their tips. Place the two thumbs upright, leaning against the sides of the index fingers.
Stand with both feet together and extend the hands backward until they are level with the forehead, with the fingertips positioned exactly between the eyebrows and hanging down toward the face.
Assume an expression of wrath. Empower white mustard seeds one hundred and eight times with the mantra, scattering one seed for each recitation while striking [the target].
Upon the ground, the earth itself opens so that those who practice the path may enter. Those who wish to dwell there and behold Maitreya may stay as they please.
If they take its wealth and emerge, they shall likewise be without fault. By eating its fruits, their lifespan shall be a thousand years.
The One-Syllable Mantra of Bhūkuṭī: Form fists by grasping each finger with the four fingers of both hands.
First place the right hand under the left armpit, then place the left hand under the right armpit.
Bend the left knee, lean the body toward the left side, and stand the right leg straight and upright. The mantra is as follows:
Oṃ (1) Piṅgaḥ (2). Having formed the mudrā, recite the Mahākāya-mantra (visualize it as the aforementioned spell) seven times.

Then withdraw the hind leg (visualize this as the left leg), placing the heel directly beneath the right knee with the foot not touching the ground. Rotate [the body] once clockwise while reciting the syllable HŪṂ.

Having uttered one sound, recite the single-syllable mantra. Looking around in all directions, manifesting a form of great wrath, and forming this dharma-seal, strike all the vajra retinues so that they are struck with great terror; all the devas, māras, and others shall be completely crushed.
The above is the Yoga Division; the following is the Buddha-uṣṇīṣa Division.
With a single mind, we reverently invoke the Dharma of the Maṇḍala of the Mantra of the One-Syllable Golden Wheel King Buddha-uṣṇīṣa (the ritual for prostration and contemplation is as before).
When the Buddha was in the kingdom of Magadha, beneath the Bodhi tree at the Vajra Seat, he subdued the four kinds of Māras and attained [enlightenment].
Regarding the unsurpassed Buddha-wisdom, at the request of the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi,
he entered the Great Samādhi of the Miraculous Transformation of the One-Syllable Cakravartin Uṣṇīṣa of All Tathāgatas. He emitted great radiance to benefit all sentient beings,
and suddenly transformed his physical appearance to become like a great Universal Monarch (Cakravartin), fully endowed with the seven treasures and surrounded by a retinue, as he sat.
Upon a white lotus flower, his physical form is brilliant and majestic, illuminating all things like a mass of molten gold. His left hand holds an opened lotus flower;
beside the calyx of the flower stands a wheel made of the seven precious jewels. Around the rim of the wheel are sharp blades, and it is encircled on the outside by flames.
His right hand has its palm raised and turned outward. The *Sūtra of the One-Syllable Heart Mantra of the Final Dharma Age* states: "At that time..."
At that time, the World-Honored One entered samādhi. From between his eyebrows, he emitted a great light.
Within that light, a voice suddenly spoke, saying: "Śākyamuni Tathāgata, I am the Single-Syllable Heart Mantra of the Universal Wheel-Turning King of Wisdom of all Tathāgatas.
[As taught by] the past Buddhas Ratnacchattra, Śālarājendra, Amitābha, and..."
The Buddhas Victorious, Wondrous Eye, Wondrous Banner, and Flower Radiance have all already spoken; you should now speak of their mudrās.
As for the form of the seal: interlace the two hands with the palms facing inward to form fists. Extend the two middle fingers, bending their upper joints into the shape of a sword.
Extend the two thumbs side by side and bend the two index fingers flat across their two joints, pressing them together against the two thumbs.
Upon the fingernail, one recites this mantra:
*Namo samantabuddhānām* (1). *Bhruṃ* (2)—the syllable *ru* is pronounced with the tongue curled back as a single sound, drawn out from the chest and throat; its resonance is like [that of a bell].
Strike the great drum. The ancient translation as "Bulin" (步林) is an erroneous and abbreviated corruption. According to this mantra, there are various versions:
some render it as "Bulong" (勃嚨), some as "Bolun" (勃琳), some as "Bulung" (部隴), some as "Beilun" (悖論), and some as "Pilang" (毗藍);
each differs from the others. All are based on the ritual manual produced by Master Kong (空師).
This ritual procedure is the most correct and most precise; it may be employed.

When this mantra is recited, the trichiliocosm shakes in six ways, Mount Sumeru, the king of mountains, also trembles greatly, the great oceans boil over, and great fires break out everywhere throughout all the palaces of the māras. Avalokiteśvara—
The Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi, through the Buddha’s majestic power, fell to the ground in a swoon. All the weapons held by the various devas likewise dropped to the earth.
At that time, the World-Honored One concealed his form as a Wheel-Turning King and resumed the appearance of a Tathāgata;
in order to cause the two bodhisattvas to rise, he spoke the Great Illuminating Mother Mantra of all Buddhas’ Eyes (namely, the mantra beginning with *Namo*...).
“Namo bhagavate... (and so forth; one mantra). The two Bodhisattvas arose, and the assembly of devas all regained their supernatural powers and returned to wielding their weapons.

The Buddha said: “If there is anyone who holds the mantra of the One-Syllable Cūḍāmaṇi King, within a distance of five yojanas, all mundane and supramundane mantras will fail to achieve siddhi. Why is this? Because [the One-Syllable King] dwells therein.”
The Samādhi of the Buddha-Uṣṇīṣa Cakravartin is such that no one can oppress or harm it.

If there are those who hold other mantras that do not manifest their efficacy, by reciting this mantra, they shall all attain accomplishment. When a practitioner wishes to perform recitation, they should first recite and hold the Buddhalocanā mantra;
thereafter, they should recite the One-Syllable Golden Wheel [mantra], and [all obstacles] will naturally become tranquil. If it is not so, [the practice will fail].
His majestic power is such that none can endure it.
With single-minded devotion, one should prostrate and pay homage to the *Sitatapatra Aparājitā Uṣṇīṣarāja Mantra Maṇḍala Dharma* (the ritual for viewing and worship is as described above).
The World-Honored One, desiring to eliminate the various karmic obstructions of all sentient beings, entered the state of all Tathāgatas.
He entered the samādhi of the Sovereign of the White Parasol Cakravartin of Measured Light.
Immediately, a single parasol manifested above his crown, completely covering the trichiliocosm; its radiance was extraordinary and its extent boundless.
He then transformed himself into the body of the Vidyārāja White Parasol Cakravartin, adorned with a circular halo and possessing a golden form.
He sits in the half-lotus posture (*ardhaparyaṅka*). His left hand holds a blossoming lotus, upon whose pedestal is a white parasol (*sitacchatra*).
His right hand holds a lotus that is half-opened and not fully opened. As for the mudrā: join the two hands with palms hollowed together;
bend the two ring fingers and insert them into the palms; then, with the faces of the two thumbs, press down upon the nails of the two ring fingers.
Bend the two index fingers so that they touch each other, forming a circle like the shape of a parasol. Recite this mantra:
Namaḥ samantabuddhānām (1) Oṃ (2) Tathāgataśrīśa (3) Anavalokitamūrdha (4) Oṃ (5) Mama mama (6)
Mā hūṃ ṇi (ni-ko, reversed). This mantra is capable of accomplishing and gathering all mantras. By the power of this king of mantras, it is unfailing and unobstructed;
it is courageous and unimpeded, for it is unequaled.
The Ritual of the Maṇḍala of the Mantra of the Sovereign Lord of the Peak of the Mass of Light (to be venerated as above).
Desiring to extinguish the evil obstructions of all sentient beings and to sever and destroy the power of mundane and supramundane mantras,
the World-Honored One entered the Great Samādhi of the Radiant Splendor of All Buddhas and proclaimed this:

The Mantra of the Sovereign of the Light-Cluster Uṣṇīṣa. This Sovereign of the Light-Cluster Uṣṇīṣa has a golden-colored body and sits upon a white lotus flower, surrounded by various kinds of light, seated amidst blazing radiance. His left hand holds an opened lotus flower;
upon the calyx of the flower is the Buddha-heart mudrā, encircled by flames. His right hand is placed at his chest, holding a [jewel].

The Intention-Mani Jewel. Its mudrā: employ the White Parasol Mudrā; separate the two index fingers and extend them straight upward, each positioned one inch and three *fen* from the tips of the middle fingers. The mantra is as follows:
Namo samanta-buddhānām (1) Oṃ (2) Tathāgata-śroṇi-śa (3) Anavalokite (4) Mūrdha (5) Tejorāśi (6) Hūṃ (7) Jvala jvala (8) Daka daka (9) Nara nara (10)
RAḤ (10) VINA RA-VINARA (11) CHINDA-CHINDA (12) BINDA-BINDA (13) HŪṂ HŪṂ PHAṬ PHAṬ (14) SVĀHĀ (15). This is the mantra of the Buddha-uṣṇīṣa King of Light-Gathering;
it is capable of severing and destroying all mundane and supramundane vidyās.

Except for the Cakravartin-uṣṇīṣa (this uṣṇīṣa is the most supreme among all mantras; it first gathers spiritual power and entirely wields the power of the One-Syllable Golden Wheel-uṣṇīṣa), the Sitātapatrā-uṣṇīṣa-rāja, the Uṣṇīṣavijayā, the Vijaya, the Buddhalocanā, and the Five-Syllable Heart Mantra of the Buddha.
It can also subdue all unruly ghosts and spirits, causing them to flee in retreat and suffer humiliation.
If one practices other mantras, one should not recite this one haphazardly, for it would diminish the majesty and power of the primary deity.
Those who wish to recite and maintain this mantra should first recite the mantra of the One-Syllable Cakravartin King and the Buddha-Eye (Buddhalocanā) mantra seven times each.
A Solemn Invocation for the Ritual of the Maṇḍala of the Mantra of the High-Crested Wheel King (the procedure for viewing is as above).
The World-Honored One, desiring to eliminate all karmic obstructions and the sufferings of sentient beings within the three realms,
entered the Samādhi of the Manifestation of the Valiant Power of All Tathāgatas and proclaimed the mantra of the High-Crested Wheel King, which is capable of—
Those great Bodhisattvas who practice with diligence attain great peace and happiness. This King Uṣṇīṣa has a halo behind his body and a golden-colored form.
His left hand is bent upward, grasping an open lotus flower; upon the center of the flower is a gold wheel with eight spokes standing upright.
His right hand holds a *kūṭaja* fruit. He sits upon a white lotus flower, following the previous root [mandala] procedure.
The mudrā (which is the same as the One-Syllable Cakravartin Mudrā; however, this requires further investigation). The two middle fingers are held straight up with their tips joined.
Among the Buddha-Usnīṣa family, this is the Abhiṣeka Mudrā. The mantra is as follows:
Namo samantabuddhānām (1) | Oṃ (2) | Jvala jvala (3) | Nyibhyo nirdagdhoṣṇīṣa (4) | Duna duna hūṃ (5).

If one practices the Cakravartin-Uṣṇīṣa or any other [rite], and wherever a person of pure faith goes to a place of dispute or litigation, they will achieve victory in all cases by reciting this mantra.
Alternatively, by wearing it upon the head, one obtains auspiciousness, majestic power, unimpeded eloquence, and immeasurable valor; all celestial Māras shall not dare to approach.
The Ritual of the Maṇḍala of the Mantra of the Supreme Buddha-Uṣṇīṣa-Cakravartin (to be viewed as above).

The World-Honored One, desiring to extinguish the various sufferings of sentient beings in all evil destinies and hells, entered the Great Samādhi of the Inconceivable Supernatural Powers of All Tathāgatas and manifested the mantra of the Supreme Uṣṇīṣa-Cakravartin. Supreme.
The King of the Uṣṇīṣa is golden in color. His left hand is at his chest, holding an open lotus flower;
upon the center of the flower stands a sword upright, surrounded by great flames. His right hand is bent outward, grasping a blue utpala lotus.
Seated in the half-lotus posture upon a white lotus flower, the mudrā is the White Parasol Mudrā:
place both index fingers upon the third joints of the two middle fingers. The mantra is as follows:
Namo samanta-buddhānām (1) Oṃ (2) Jvala jayūṣṇiṣa (3) Jvala jvala (4) Buddhanama buddhanama (5) Nruma nruma nruma (6) Haḥ (7)
When this mantra— HĀ HŪṂ (drawn out)—
is recited, the great trichiliocosm shakes, and the intense sufferings of all the evil beings in the hells are completely stilled.
All those hungry ghosts shall obtain food of ambrosia. Those who uphold this [teaching] will be revered by devas and humans;
possessing a body of inconceivable merit, they will be able to manifest supernormal powers, enter the hells, and liberate all sentient beings from their manifold sufferings.
The Ritual for the Maṇḍala of the Image of the Tathāgata Ratnaketu, the Wheel-Turning King (the method for reverent viewing is as above).

Regarding the *Uṣṇīṣavijaya*: if sentient beings possess little power of progress or wisdom and are unable to uphold the vast image-dharma, they should take white woolen cloth whose threads have not yet been cut and paint the World-Honored One, the Tathāgata Ratnaketu, turning the wheel of the Dharma.
The image of a Wheel-Turning King (Cakravartin). His body is golden in color. He forms the mudrā of preaching the Dharma and sits in the full lotus posture upon a white lotus flower.
His entire body radiates a blazing brilliance, from which many wheels emerge; light also issues forth from the crown of his head.
On the seat, depict the Brahma King and the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi. Behind them, at the top, paint mountain peaks.

In the sky, depict two princes with flower garlands. Below, on the right side, paint the practitioner in his natural form, holding an incense burner and assuming a posture of gazing up toward the World-Honored One.
This is the most supreme painting method for the Cakravartin Buddha-Uṣṇīṣa. [End of] Image.
Within the offering altar, facing west, perform incense burning and recitation three times each day for one million repetitions.

Only after this should you perform the ritual procedure. Whenever reciting, first perform the five-limb yoga (that is, empower the crown of the head, the two shoulders, the heart, and the throat with the mantra) to achieve the yoga of the deity.
Next, visualize a single syllable placed in three locations upon your own body (the Sanskrit syllable *Oṃ* placed on the crown of the head; the Sanskrit [syllable]...).

Place *Āḥ* upon the tongue; place the *Hūṃ* of the Brahmī script upon the heart). By the power of these seed-syllables (*bīja*), one is able to become the Honored One, the Cakravartin of the Buddha’s Crown.
Next, visualize that within the maṇḍala there is a great ocean of fragrant water.
In the center of that ocean is Mount Sumeru, surrounded on all sides by seven tiers of golden mountains. Atop the summit of Mount Sumeru is a white eight-petaled lotus flower.
Upon each individual petal, arrange the seven treasures of a universal monarch (cakravartin)—namely, the golden wheel, elephant, horse, jewel, woman, military retinue, and treasury.
On the eighth petal, which stands before [the center], visualize the Honored One Locanā, surrounded in front and behind by the retinue of the ten Buddha-uṣṇīṣas.
Then, holding the rosary, perform the recitation with proper visualization, fixing the mind on the tip of the nose without the slightest distraction.

Chaos may arise, whether by the hundreds, thousands, or even tens of thousands; yet once the daily limit of practice is completed, one should hold the *japa*-beads above the head and recite the mantra of the Mother of the Family (*kulamātṛ*) for the dedication of merit.
May the Honored One protect all such meritorious deeds. This method of contemplative practice is praised by all Buddhas.
If, during these thirty-six months, one refrains from all idle talk and does not allow the mind to wander toward other objects, then one shall attain [the goal].
The Gate of Direct Realization of the Great Samādhi of the One-Syllable Cakravartin (the image faces east and the person faces west; this is the correct orientation).
If one performs the rite of pacification (*śāntika*), perform *homa* with clarified butter, burning it one by one; thus one attains the accomplishment of the dharma.
If one performs *homa* with curd, one obtains increase (*puṣṭika*). If one performs *homa* with *kūrca* grass, one causes the attainment of increased longevity.
If one performs homa with honey, all people will become respectful and affectionate toward them. If one performs homa with milk, one will attain majestic power and virtue.
If one performs homa with non-glutinous rice, one will obtain children. If one performs homa with sesame seeds, whatever wealth and treasures one seeks will be obtained.
If one performs homa with black mustard seeds, one will be able to subdue and conquer enemies.
If one is afflicted by a ghostly illness, form the mudrā and recite the mantra; for each repetition, further add the syllable *phaṭ*.
For those suffering from insect venom, medicinal poison, distress, pain, or being on the verge of death, recite this mantra;
for each repetition, add the two syllables *jñā* seven times, then add the three syllables *mo ma mo* seven times, and finally add the syllable *si*.
Seven times. Furthermore, add the two characters "zhā" (pronounced like "tà") and "mù" seven times. Thus are the added characters.
Recite all [mantras] silently with the voice; restrain and prohibit the poisons so that they may not function.

One will recover from confusion and fainting. If restraining a ghost, add the recitation of *tiṣṭha tiṣṭha* within the mantra, or add *kaca kaca* (the *ka* is pronounced as *gu-na*), or add *rukṣa rukṣa*; thus one restrains the body.
To perform the rite of immobilization, one may add the syllables *luṇḍa luṇḍa*. This will cause the breath in the throat of a ghost to be blocked so that it cannot escape.
If a person is bitten by a snake, draw the form of a snake holding a sword. Recite the mantra once and cut [the drawing] once; the snake that bit the person will immediately come.
By rotating the sword counter-clockwise, the snake is dispatched and sent back. Furthermore, recite the mantra while taking refuge.
Add two *hūṃ* syllables; this will immediately restrain the snake and cause it to submit. If one recites the mantra while chanting the *hūṃ* syllable, it will result in its release.
Add two *phaṭ* syllables and recite the mantra while drawing on the ground with the left thumb;
the snake that bit the person will immediately come. Omit the *phaṭ* syllables and recite [the mantra] twenty-one times, then touch the forehead with the hand. As for that...

The person who was bitten will immediately rise. Recite the mantra twenty-one times over water and swirl it above the head like a wheel, while simultaneously reciting the *phaṭ* mantra twenty-one times. Take water for the nose, empower it, and scatter it in the four directions.
Then go to one's own dwelling, take water, empower it as before, and throw it downward upon the ground. Return once more.

Craving, ignorance, false discrimination, and the afflictions of the three poisons arise from a failure to comprehend the true nature of reality;
these are the conditions summoned by the accumulation of unwholesome karma. One should construct a square mandala measuring five cubits, arranged in three tiers.
In the center is an eight-petaled lotus flower, upon which is painted the Bodhisattva Mahāmāyūrī Vidyārājñī, facing eastward, her body white in color.
Appearance: She wears a light garment of white silk, adorned with a crown, necklaces, earrings, and armlets.
Adorned in various ornaments, she rides upon a golden peacock king and sits atop a white lotus flower. She abides in the mudrā of compassion and has four arms.
Her first right hand holds a blossoming lotus; her second hand holds a *kūṭaja* fruit (resembling a papaya). Her first left...

The [first] hand should be at the heart, holding an auspicious fruit (shriphala) shaped like a peach. The second hand holds three or five peacock feathers upon a lotus petal, spiraling counter-clockwise from the right.
On these lotus petals, paint the seven World-Honored Buddhas; on the eighth petal in the northwest [is the remaining one].
Paint an image of Maitreya; all [the figures] shall have their heads facing outward, each abiding in a posture of meditative concentration (*samādhi*).
On the four sides of the inner court, outside the flower petals, paint four Pratyekabuddhas. In the four corners, paint the four great Śrāvakas (Ānanda, Rāhula, Śāriputra, and Maudgalyāyana).
In the second court, paint the eight celestial kings (*lokapāla*) together with their retinues.

In the third court, paint the twenty-eight yakṣa generals and the deities of the twelve zodiacal mansions (*nakṣatra-rāśi*). To the east of the maṇḍala, install an image of the Buddha-mother Mahāmāyūrī Vidyārājñī.
As for the method of painting this image, it is the same as the previous images, except that the boundary lines (*sīmā*) are not drawn (this is the primary deity image for the second seat).

Perform the offerings according to the ritual protocol. There should be three to five, up to seven, readers of the scriptures who shall alternate day and night so that the sound of the recitation does not cease.
Only one person shall serve as a master of the teachings and mantras, well-versed in the doctrine, to direct the proceedings and manage the distribution of items.
Regarding the ritual procedure for responding to the deities: one should form mudrās and invoke the sages and worthies. Other participants should simply recite the sutras with a sincere mind;
the essential points lie in the high frequency of recitation and the earnestness of their vows.

Following the thirty-sevenfold holy liturgy of repentance, whether at three sessions or six sessions, the duration of the ritual site may be one day, two or three days, or even up to seven days. (Ming Dynasty)

They should go to private homes and set the scriptural texts to musical melodies, accompanied by bells, cymbals, flutes, and strings; this is called "playing the Peacock Sutra," which may be described as irreverent and profane.

When the Buddha was in the palace of the Nāga Kings Nanda and Upananda,
he accepted the invitation of the Great Nāga King Anantavyūha-samudra-megha-tejo-rāja-cchattra and taught the empowerment and majestic adornment born of the Great Cloud.
The Tathāgata named Vairocana-Śrī-Kanaka-Raśmi-Vajra-Padma-Sambhava-Jñāna-Dhvaja,
who arises from a single hair-tip and belongs to that lineage— should all nāgas be able to uphold his name, invoke it, and pay him homage,
they shall all be liberated from every suffering and hardship, and he will immediately cause rain to fall within this Jambudvīpa.
Sweet rain falls; medicinal herbs, thickets, forests, trees, and crops all flourish and grow.

By the true power of all Tathāgatas, Arhats, Samyaksaṃbuddhas—such as Flying Cloud, Majestic Virtue, Radiant Cloud Light, and all others—and by the true power of all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas, I command all the nāgas to send down great rain within this Jambudvīpa and to eliminate the five obstacles to rain. (The mudrā is to be examined. The mantra is as follows:
Tadyathā (1) | Svara svara (2) | Hiri hiri (3) | Sulū sulū (4) | Nāgānām (5) | Japa japa (6) | Śapi śapi (7) | Śuphu śuphu (8) | Chala (9).
(By the power of the Buddha’s true strength, may the great dragon kings and others quickly come here to this place of prayer within Jambudvīpa and pour down great rain. Chala.
Cela (both with departing tone) (1); Jili jili (2); Zhulou zhulou (3); Svāhā (4). (This mantra text is very long;

the Sui translation includes both Chinese and Sanskrit, while the Tang translation preserves only the Sanskrit sounds. These few lines are what is commonly recited for the prayer for rain. If performing the ritual by constructing a maṇḍala, one should recite the full text.
One who wishes to invoke rain should construct a twelve-cubit maṇḍala on open ground and place a high seat in its center. Upon it...
Spread a new blue mat and hang a blue canopy. Three cubits to the east of the seat, using cow dung juice, draw a three-headed nāga king surrounded by various nāgas.
Five cubits to the south, draw a five-headed nāga king surrounded by various nāgas. Seven cubits to the west, draw a seven-headed nāga king.
Nine cubits to the north, one should paint a nine-headed nāga king surrounded by all the other nāgas.
In each of the four corners, place four flower vases; mix gold-essence stone with lampblack and water until they are blue, filling all the vases completely. Insert flower stamens into the vases.
At each of the four gates, install incense burners and burn various kinds of incense. Hang blue banners on each of the four sides.
There are seven [sets], totaling twenty-eight banners, each one zhang in length. Furthermore, ghee lamps shall be lit in accordance with the number of banners.
Various fruits, ghee, curds, and milk porridge are to be set out before the various dragon kings at the four sides. Flowers are to be scattered and incense burned without interruption.
The fruit, food, vessels, and garments must be new every day; old items are not permitted to be used. At the beginning of the day...
When setting out, one should prepare the ritual offerings. The person reciting the sūtra shall bathe three times a day and wear fresh blue robes.
First, they should pay homage to all Buddhas, burn incense, and scatter flowers, inviting all Buddhas, the great Bodhisattvas, and all devas and nāga kings.
For the sake of sentient beings, they must constantly give rise to a mind of loving-kindness, never conceiving evil thoughts. With this reverence—

Having dedicated the merit of the Buddha and all his virtues to all the great Dragon Kings as well as to all sentient beings, he then ascended the seat and recited the sutra in a loud voice, continuing day and night without ceasing for either seven days or twenty-one days;
thus, sweet rain will surely fall. (The mantras of all Tathāgatas appearing in the Great Canon’s Secret Essentials have been recorded herein; body, speech, and mind are themselves the maṇḍala.)
The Ritual of the Maṇḍala for the Mantra of Vajrajvālā to Cease Wind and Rain (Method of Viewing as Above).
While the Buddha was traveling through the kingdom of Magadha, he encountered dark clouds, fierce winds, thunder, and lightning on the road.
The Buddha instructed Ānanda to take a new, clean jar, fill it with water, and subdue the evil dragon by causing it to enter the jar. Then, raising his voice, [the Buddha] recited the mantra.
Mantra: [Recite] with a water jar, its mouth inverted, placed over the altar in the open air; this will stop the wind and rain.
Furthermore, the mantra of Pīṭhaka is spoken as follows: (The hand seal has not been transmitted; one should instead use the vajra-fist.)
Namo buddhāya (1) | Namo dharmāya (2) | Namo saṃghāya (3) | Tadyathā (4) | Oṃ (5) | Kha-ra kha-ra kha-ra kha-ra (6) | Kha kha kha kha kha kha kha kha (7) | Namaḥ kaśyapāya tathāgatāya (8).
(9) *Araṅkate samyaksambuddhāya* | (10) *Siddham* | (11) *Mantrapadāya svāhā* | (12) When the evil dragons sent down torrential rain for a long time without clearing,
[the practitioner] prepared the altar on the ground along the path and gathered one thousand and eighty seasonal flowers.
Take one *dō* (flower) and offer it to the Buddha; then perform the *homa* rite with these flowers. Recite with a loud, rapid voice, casting one flower for each recitation.
Once these flowers are exhausted, all evil winds and torrential rains will immediately clear and cease.

If there are heavy obstructions such that the weather does not clear after one attempt, repeat the practice from one to two, and so on up to five times according to the ritual rules; there is nothing that will not be [resolved].
Regarding "clear weather": the practitioner must bathe to purify the body and attire, cease all speech and discourse, and remain in accord with a mind of great compassion;
thus, one will attain accomplishment.
Furthermore, there is the root heart-mantra.
*Namo buddhāya* (1). *Oṃ hrīṃ hrīṃ* (2). *Candre hrīṃ* (3). *Candra candra mandaye* (4). *Svāhā* (5). This is the heart mantra (*hṛdaya-mantra*).
If there is anyone who can believe, understand, receive, and uphold it, and who dwells upon the summit of a high mountain, by means of this—
Recite the mantra one hundred and eight times to consecrate a branch of pomegranate.

Holding a staff in the right hand and forming the nāga-king mudrā with the left, gaze upon the heavens and earth, the fields and the crops in the ten directions, while uttering a roar of fierce wrath.

Recite the mantra once and brandish the staff as if to strike once; by doing this for a fixed period, reciting it one thousand and eighty times in total, all evil and poisonous dragons and the like will have their body hairs stand on end, trembling with fear and unease.

Their poisonous intent will be extinguished, and they will be restrained from causing evil winds, rains, thunder, lightning, and thunderbolts. Regarding the "Dragon-Sitting Seal," use the left hand...
The thumbs are bent across within the palms. The middle and ring fingers are bent down to press upon the thumbs.

The index fingers are extended straight with a slight bend. The little fingers are extended straight without being bent. (Those essential points not previously collected are supplemented here in this later compilation.)
A Solemn Invocation for the Dharma of the Secret Mantra Maṇḍala of the Great Jewel Vast Pavilion of Secure Abiding (to be viewed as above). The World-Honored One,
turning the Wheel of Dharma once again, by the power of samādhi, proceeded to the world-system of Ratnapradīpa to the exquisite Maṇi.
Having established various pure abodes for the Tathāgata, he commanded the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi, the Lord of Secrets, to strike the earth with his vajra.
From the place where it split open, a pavilion made of the seven precious gems surged forth, and within the pavilion appeared a stūpa.
Within it were the bodies of three Tathāgatas: the first was named Maṇiratnakusumadhvaja-rāja Tathāgata;
the second, Citramaṇi Tathāgata; and the third, Vajrābhyudgatarāja Tathāgata. These three Buddhas, in a past eon, were three rishis who dwelt upon a mountain of jewels.
With right mindfulness, they contemplated: "What [means] and at what time will we be able..."
He attained perfect enlightenment and delivered all sentient beings. Then, from the heavens, the deities of the Śuddhāvāsa Heaven proclaimed:
"In the past, all Tathāgatas, desiring to benefit sentient beings, have taught the Great Jewel Vast and Secure Secret Dhāraṇī.
Upon merely hearing this mantra, one shall attain non-retrogression toward unsurpassed bodhi and all the Buddha-dharmas."
When [the realization] was attained and manifested before him, the Rishi rejoiced. At his dwelling place, he then relinquished his life;
his body, like fresh ghee, melted and dissolved into the earth. From the very spot where he vanished, three bamboos sprang up.
After growing for ten months, they split open of their own accord, and within each appeared a youth, with exceptionally radiant complexion and endowed with the marks and signs of perfection. Thus...

Beneath the bamboo, he sat cross-legged and entered into right concentration. On the seventh day, during the middle watch of the night, he attained equal and perfect enlightenment (*samyak-saṃbodhi*).
At that time, those three bamboos all transformed into pavilions made of the seven precious jewels.
Furthermore, in the midst of space, there appeared the Great Jewel Vast Pavilion of the Secret Dhāraṇī of Good Abiding, with gold as its [foundation].
The name [appears]. Suddenly manifesting in the pure abodes within the sky, he is none other than Śākyamuni.
Furthermore, there is an attendant named Pure Abode (Viśuddhāvāsa) who constantly and diligently serves him and receives the Buddha’s prediction;
this is precisely this majestic Maṇi-establishment Tathāgata. Regarding the mudrā of the root mantra: join the right hand’s index finger with the thumb. With...
Press the tip of the right index finger against the side of the left index finger; do the same with the left hand. Join the two hands in *añjali* at the heart.
Then, slightly bend the middle fingers of both hands so that their tips touch one another. Next, extend the ring fingers of both hands.
One should also cause the two hands to support each other. Extend the left and right little fingers of each hand. The mantra is as follows:
Namo sarvatathāgatānām (1) Oṃ (2) Vipulagarbhe (3) Maṇiprabhe (4) Tattvataḥ (5) Nirdaśane (6) Maṇi (7)
Maṇi (7) | Supratiṣṭhe (8) | Vimale (9) | Śāntanirvṛte (10) | Hūṃ (11) | Hūṃ (12) | Jvala (13) | Buddhavilokite (14) | Guhyatejodgate (15) | Svāhā (16) ||
(17) Again, interlock the right thumb with the index finger and extend the remaining three fingers, placing them over the heart. Then,
interlock the left thumb with the little finger and extend the remaining three fingers, covering the knees with the palms facing upward.
Pointing downward, extend the fingers straight and level; this is called the "Consoling Hand. Recite the Heart Mantra:
Oṃ vajri hūṃ. Then, with the right hand, join the thumb and ring finger together, extend the remaining three fingers, and place the palm upward upon the knee.
Again, with the left hand, join the thumb and little finger together and extend the remaining three fingers to cover the heart.
Then, with the right hand, place the thumb at the tip of the ring finger and hold it horizontally across the heart, extending the other three fingers.
Place the left hand palm-up on the left knee, bending the first joint of the thumb while extending all the other fingers. This is the *cittamantra* (Heart Mantra).
It is said:
(1) Oṃ, (2) Maṇidhare, (3) Hūṃ Phaṭ (half-syllable).
Upon a white cloth, one should paint a pavilion adorned with the seven treasures; within the pavilion, one should paint the Tathāgata.
He expounds the characteristics of phenomena (*dharmalakṣaṇa*) while seated upon a lion throne. To the right, paint Vajrapāṇi with twelve arms, of a yellowish-white complexion.
His image has four faces: the front face is joyful; the left face is wrathful; the right face has its mouth agape, with canine teeth protruding upward.
Above his head, he has a furrowed brow and angry eyes; his crown is adorned with various ornaments.
Upon a lotus flower, he sits in the half-lotus posture (*ardhaparyaṅka*). To his left is painted the Bodhisattva Ratnavajra, who has four faces and sixteen arms.
His primary face is joyful; the right face is blue, having the countenance of Mahākāla; the left face is green, having the countenance of a teacher...
The face of the Son: on the upper part of the head, with knitted brows and bared teeth, of a pale green color, seated in the half-lotus posture upon a lotus flower.
Below Vajrapāṇi, one should paint Śrīdevī; behind her, paint the goddess Vajradūtī.
Below the Jewel-Vajra, paint the goddess Śaṅkhinī; behind her, paint the goddess Puṣpadantī.
In front of the Buddha, paint a flower made of the seven precious gems; this flower has a hundred petals, with a golden pedestal and a stem of vaidūrya.
Upon the flower is a wheel with a hundred spokes, surrounded by a halo of light. Above the root of the flower, paint the Four Great Kings, clad in armor and holding their weapons. Below...
Paint a pond. On its bank, paint a practitioner of recitation holding an incense burner, flower branches, and a rosary, kneeling and gazing up at the Tathāgata.
In the empty space above a jeweled pavilion, paint Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Maheśvara scattering flowers as an offering.
If one maintains the root mantra, there is no need to select specific days or times.
Regarding the constellations and planets (*nakṣatra-graha*): without being restricted by fasting or ritual observances, recite [the mantra] ten thousand times in its entirety.

From the eighth to the fifteenth day of the waxing moon (*śuklapakṣa*), bathe with purity, wear fresh clean garments, and make offerings according to one's means. Recite it three times a day, one hundred and eight times each time.
One may immediately rest and sleep in that very place. When daybreak approaches, the Tathāgata will manifest his body, and Vajrapāṇi will also appear.

Whatever aspirations one has shall all be fulfilled as desired. All calamities of water or fire, enemies, thieves, poison, harm, and serious illnesses—including diseases of the eyes, ears, nose, tongue, mouth, teeth, lips, head, limbs, and joints, whether mild or severe fevers—all [shall be pacified].
One will not be harmed by physical ailments, nor by venomous snakes, tigers, wolves, malevolent incantations, or curses. If one recites or chants this mantra—
where "reading" refers to following the text word-for-word and "chanting" refers to repeating it twice— if one wears it upon the body, paints it upon clothing, places it atop a banner,
writes it in a scripture, or inscribes it on silk, wool, walls, or wooden tablets, then all who see or hear it [shall be protected].

Furthermore, those who pass through its shadow, or those who briefly touch the practitioner, or those who are touched by others who have been so touched—all such beings shall certainly attain non-retrogression from unsurpassed bodhi.
They shall be able to obtain immeasurable merit in this present life, remain far removed from all [negative] karma, and accomplish roots of virtue. This applies if they accomplish the Heart Mantra.
The practitioner: by reciting one hundred thousand times, one immediately beholds all Tathāgatas; by reciting two hundred thousand times, one attains vision of all Buddha-fields;
by reciting three hundred thousand times, all mantra-dharmas are accomplished;
by reciting four hundred thousand times, one becomes a Cakravartin among the Vidyādharas; by reciting five hundred thousand times, [one gains access to] all the caves of the ṛṣis.
One enters the dragon caves and the asura caves in their entirety; at sixty thousand recitations, one beholds all hidden treasures;
at seventy thousand recitations, one immediately recollects and knows the events of immeasurable past lives;
at eighty thousand recitations, one immediately attains the *ratnamudrā-samādhi*; and at ninety thousand recitations, one attains the playful mastery of all bodhisattvas.
Through the empowerment of supernormal powers, by reciting this one million times, one obtains the consecration of all Tathāgatas and enters the assembly of all Tathāgatas.
By multiplying it in this manner, one attains immeasurable and most excellent merits. If one desires to bring rain:
Take white mustard seeds and empower them one thousand and eight times. Scatter them into the air, and rain will fall immediately.

If one is suffering from a grave illness, this shall also bring about recovery. Take one bottle of water and place inside it equal parts of *vidanga*, red ochre, white mustard seeds, turmeric, and white sandalwood.

Empower it ten thousand times and pour it over the crown of the patient’s head; all grave illnesses will be cured, and all written talismans or malevolent incantations will be completely neutralized. For those with epilepsy, leprosy, or white leprosy (*sidhma*), bathing and consecrating the head with this water will likewise bring about recovery.
Furthermore, if a woman seeks a son, she shall be granted a male child by using the aforementioned medicinal water with mantras for consecration (*abhiṣeka*).
If one recites the *Cittamantra* ten thousand times, all obstructing spirits and deities will come to prostrate at one's feet; at twenty thousand recitations, [the same occurs].
Just as the words spoken by the Lord of the Devas are all obeyed and put into practice, so it is at thirty thousand recitations:
the spirits, ghosts, and yakṣas are all brought into submission. At forty thousand recitations, all summonings are accomplished according to one’s will.
At fifty thousand recitations, humans and devas are summoned and all follow my intent. At sixty thousand recitations, one attains the stainless samādhi. At seventy thousand recitations...
At eighty thousand recitations, one becomes a wheel-turning king among the vidyādhara-siddhas, and the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi together with his retinue will appear before one.
At ninety thousand recitations, all bodhisattvas will grant one fearlessness.
At one hundred thousand recitations, one will see all buddhas, reach all buddha-fields, master all sūtras and śāstras, and attain non-retrogression from *samyak-saṃbodhi*.
It is approved by all the Tathāgatas of the ten directions.

With a single mind, one should reverently invoke the Vairocana Tathāgata’s Great Wisdom Fist Seal Mantra Maṇḍala Rite (the ritual for prostration and contemplation is as above). [The seal-form is as seen previously.]
If one forms mudrās and recites mantras while placing them upon the body of a sick person, that illness will be cured immediately. If placed upon the heart, all poisons will be eliminated;
even malevolent seals and other such methods will be utterly destroyed. If placed upon the sense faculties, the faculties will become complete.

If it revolves around the body, one will attain great eloquence. If, after reciting the name of the Buddha, one rotates it through the various directions and then places it [upon the body], [the same benefits shall follow].
The fundamental mind—whether for one’s own accomplishment or for the sake of others—attains great joy and bliss until the realization of Bodhi.
Oṃ (1) Hūṃ (2). If one binds this mudrā and visualizes the Buddhas, one should understand that the five aggregates are like a potter’s wheel; thereafter, the body...
Perform prostrations, recite the mantra with the mouth, and contemplate correctly with a single mind.
Abiding in the ten perfections, give rise to the gates of dhāraṇī, fulfill the practices of the ten stages, the ten unhindered understandings, and the eighteen unique qualities.
Through the method of Viśvakarman, benefit all sentient beings; through the three vajra-actions, perform the great Buddha-work.
The Ritual of the Maṇḍala for the Mantra of Auspiciousness and the Elimination of Calamities of the Tathāgata Sālarāja (Prostrations and Contemplation as Above).
The Buddha Sālarāja of the Past possesses the Great Buddha-uṣṇīṣa Tejorāśi Mantra for the Elimination of Calamities and Auspiciousness.
Should kings, ministers, their retinues, and all the common people be oppressed by the five planets, Rāhu, Ketu, comets, meteors, or malevolent stars;
or if the throne of the Emperor is assailed, causing calamities to arise in succession for the state, the family, or the specific regions and asterisms to which they belong;
or if Saturn should assail them, creating various obstacles and difficulties—then, simply by...
In a pure place, establish a *maṇḍala* and recite this mantra one hundred and eight times, or one thousand times.
Whether for one day, two days, three days, or up to seven days, recite and maintain it with single-minded devotion; all calamities and misfortunes will be entirely extinguished.

If a person has many obstacles, such as a woman suffering a difficult childbirth or being afflicted by spirits and ghosts, one should fashion a mantra-cord from five-colored threads and tie it around the patient’s neck, hands, feet, waist, and abdomen.
One should also fashion a single image of Bhaisajyaguru and transcribe one scroll of the sutra.
Construct one banner made of five colors, forty-nine feet in length.

May all that is sought be fulfilled as desired.
If one knows that there are obstacles or hindrances, one should take various types of incense, blend them together, and smear them upon the image. Furthermore, bathe the image with scented water.
Once the bathing of the image is complete, collect the water again and perform the empowerment (*adhitiṣṭhati*) one hundred and eight times before the image.
Bathe the entire body with it; obstacles and difficulties will be extinguished.
If one suffers from a malarial fever lasting one day, two days, three days, or four days, reciting this will bring immediate recovery.
For those struck by ghosts, or afflicted by epilepsy, scrofula, leprosy, or *gudu* (poisonous charms), empower earth and mustard seeds with mantras and mix them with white sandalwood;
apply this to the body seventeen times and they will be immediately healed.
For those afflicted by malignant winds (*vāta*), apply oil empowered by mantra; they will be cured immediately.
For earaches, blend *śrīkhaṇḍa* (sandalwood) oil with birch bark and boil it; empower it and drop it into the ear.
The pain will cease at once. This also cures hemicrania.
Regarding all illnesses and ailments, as soon as one recites this empowerment, there are none that are not cured.
Even without prior practice or cultivation, one will be able to accomplish all undertakings.

First, the Mudrā of Wrathful Countenance (Standing with feet together and toes aligned. Bend the little finger of the left hand and press it beneath the thumb. Spread the remaining three fingers straight out. Place these three fingers upon the forehead in a wrathful manner.

With the right hand, cross the webbed space at the right hip, with the four fingers pointing forward toward the face. This mudrā can subdue all evil māras and non-Buddhists; one shall be entirely fearless. While performing this mudrā:)
All ghosts and spirits shall forever cease to exist. Second is the Mudrā of High Pride (following the previous procedure;

however, change the left hand so that the index, middle, and ring fingers are bent into the palm, while the thumb and little finger remain extended. Bend the tip of the index finger at the middle joint so it is level with the tip of the thumb, leaving a space of about two inches.

Place this against the space between the eyebrows with the tips of the fingers pointing downward. Maintain a broad and forbearing expression on the face; do not show a form of anger. If one binds this mudrā, all sentient beings of the six realms shall be liberated from all suffering and hardship).
The Third Face: The Great Wrathful Seal (Perform as before; however, change only the left thumb by bending it toward the palm. Curl the middle, ring, and little fingers to embrace it.

Extend the index finger straight, with the tip of the index finger pointing toward the mouth, but not touching it. Move the tongue and the index finger simultaneously. Form a face of great wrath. By performing this seal-method, all demonic illnesses shall be completely cured).

The fourth is the Seal of the Soft Heart (pronounced *ruan*): [Stand as before; with the left hand, cross it at the side of the left waist. With the right hand, bend the index, ring, and little fingers toward the palm.]

Press the head with the thumb and place it upon the index finger. Extend the middle finger straight, touching the space between the eyebrows, with the tip of the middle finger pointing downward. Maintain a broad and serene expression on the face; do not display an angry countenance. Practice this daily, burning incense as an offering.
Then Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva will rejoice and grant all desires according to one’s wishes, so that everything may be fulfilled to one’s satisfaction.

The Fifth: The Mudrā of Great Wrathful Face (*Mahākrodhamukha*). (Stand as before; however, change the right hand so that the middle finger is held straight upright. Use the index finger to strike the back of the middle finger, with the tip resting upon the upper joint and both [fingers] slightly bent.

The ring finger and little finger are slightly curved. The tips of the middle and ring fingers are separated by about two inches. The thumb is held straight upright; the tip of the thumb and the tip of the middle finger are separated by about four inches.

Place the tip of the thumb upon the crown of the head. The tip of the middle finger points forward and must not touch the head. If one binds this mudrā, all evil persons, malevolent spirits, and ghosts will have their minds transformed, turning instead toward a benevolent heart.)

The Sixth: The Seal for Rebuking and Expelling (Stand as before; however, bend only the right arm so that the joints protrude outward at an angle. Extend all five fingers together and hold the palms horizontally, with the side of the thumb placed against the chest but not touching it.

If treating demonic illnesses, perform this seal by striking to the right with the palm while burning incense daily. By performing this seal, all evil obstacles and difficulties shall be utterly extinguished).
The Mudrā of Victory over the Seventh Face (Stand as before. With both left and right hands, bend each thumb into the palm and enclose it with the middle, ring, and little fingers.

Bring the tips of the left and right index fingers together at their sides; join the middle phalanges of the backs of the left and right middle, ring, and little fingers. Position this above the eyebrows, then turn it over so that the tips of the index fingers point downward.
If one performs this mudrā, all ghosts, spirits, devas, and others will be subdued and struck with terror. It should be used for curing diseases).

The Eighth Face: The Supreme Seal (*Paramamudrā*). (One should stand upright with the two feet separated by about two shaku. The toes should be aligned side-by-side. The middle fingers of both hands are bent at the middle joints and placed within the palms. Next, the two thumbs are pressed down upon them.

The index and ring fingers of both hands have their tips touching the sides of the fingers, while the little fingers are spread apart. The wrists are joined. The lower joints of the two thumbs are placed against the forehead, with the tips of the fingers pointing upward.

If a great wind or rain arises during the performance of a major merit-field ritual (*puṇyakṣetra*), one should bind this seal and recite the mantra one hundred and eight times. Regarding the Ninth Face, the Seal of the Unassailable: one should stand upright with the heels and toes of both feet touching each other. Greatly bend the knees of both legs, remaining in a posture that is neither fully seated nor standing.

In both hands, join the index and little fingers, bending them into the palms so that the backs of their middle joints touch. Stand the two index fingers upright with their tips leaning against each other; the tips of the two thumbs should also touch, resting against the sides of the middle fingers. With this—

First, place it upon the chest. Next, raise the mudrā: place the middle, ring, and little fingers of both hands upon the forehead, with the tips of the index fingers pointing upward. When the Bodhisattva performs this mudrā, all devas, māras, and spirits shall fall prostrate to the ground.
Perform this daily, making various kinds of offerings; it can prolong one's lifespan, and at the end of life, one will be reborn in the Land of Amitābha Buddha. Tenth:

The Seal of the Invincible Face (Standing on the ground, first bend the left knee deeply and straighten the calf to press against the ground with the toes pointing forward. Extend the right leg obliquely and straightly toward the right side with the toes pointing forward.

Interlace the left and right hands behind the back, with the index fingers and ring fingers inside the palms, the right pressing down upon the left. The little fingers and middle fingers of both hands touch their tips together, and both thumbs are held upright and parallel, not touching the head.)

Place the sides of the fingers together at the wrists and raise the mudrā to rest upon the right armpit; recite the mantra seven times. At the conclusion, raise it again to rest upon the forehead and recite it another seven times.
In whatever land this rite is performed, the five grains will flourish, the people will be free from illness, and one will be able to destroy all the teachings of the non-Buddhists.

Eleventh: The Mudrā for Destroying the Māra Army (Join the wrists. Extend the left thumb and little finger together, and likewise the right; bend the index, middle, and ring fingers so that their tips are about one inch apart.

Open the sides of the fingertips of each finger by about half an inch. Raise them and place them beneath the wrists upon the crown of the head. Bend the right knee as in the previous body mudrā; extend the left knee, also as in the previous body mudrā).

the methods for concealing one's form at will, various methods for medicinal herbs, the methods for the ritual pestle, the methods for the ritual vase, and all other desired mundane and supramundane dharmas— all shall be accomplished.

First is the medicinal amulet. Take equal parts of ox-gall, white sandalwood, turmeric, camphor, musk, clove, white cardamom, the filaments of red lotus, the leaves of blue lotus, gold leaf, and white honey.
Pound them together into pills while reciting the mantra during the pounding. At the time of a solar or lunar eclipse, place the medicine before the image and recite it repeatedly.

Recite the mantra. As long as the medicinal herbs do not cease [their efficacy], and if the three signs appear, one may immediately take them for use; this is the same as the methods of the various families (*kula*).

Like the orb of the sun, which all people delight to behold, even if one is to be executed, by fumigating and wearing the medicine, the executioner's strength will break into pieces and the body shall attain liberation. However, it is poisonous and must not be taken recklessly.
Second is the "Oral Amulet" (*kavaca*). Take camphor, musk, *gavāṃśṛṅga* (ox-horn), and *gorocanā* (cow-gallstone), blend them together, and grind them into a fine powder.
Mix with rainwater and form pills the size of *bimbi* (walnut) seeds. Perform the ritual during a solar or lunar eclipse.
If the medicine is accomplished, place it in the mouth; then whatever one seeks will be attained without fail.
Third is the eye medicine: take realgar, *Cirsium arvense* seeds (cang-er-zi), and burn them to collect the liquid extract;

then combine and grind together red lotus stamens, blue lotus leaves, ox-gall (*gorocana*), *uśīra*, dried ginger, *deodar* (or, according to some, elephant bile), *pippalī*, black pepper, and sea foam. Furthermore, add musk, camphor, and raw white stone honey.
Reduce each of the aforementioned ingredients by half, blend them thoroughly, and grind them finely. Place the mixture in a copper vessel and set it before the image.
One may also perform this rite during a solar or lunar eclipse; according to the signs that appear, one will attain superior, middling, or inferior accomplishments.
Taking some of the substance and applying it to the eyes, its efficacy is exceedingly vast.
If there is a drought, one should perform homa according to the ritual for three days and three nights using white mustard seeds mixed with clarified butter;
